title: C2280C — Body control module (BCM) connector
introduction:
The body control module coordinates many body electrical functions, and this connector map shows how varied that guest list can be: lighting, locks, protected supplies and grounds all appear here. I use the drawing like a seating chart. The cavity label gives the location in the illustration; the matching table row tells me which recorded circuit belongs there.

Start with the harness identification, then read Cavity across to Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Terminal Part Number. Keep the Function wording precise: driver unlock is distinct from passenger-door unlock excluding the driver, and all-lock is another assignment. Supply descriptions retain the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative; they do not choose a protective device for the vehicle. A relay label describes a switching function and does not guarantee a separate plug-in relay.

The drawing’s numbering runs in bands around a long central rectangular housing feature, so follow the printed labels rather than assuming a simple left-to-right sequence. Grey-filled circles align with rows that have blank circuit details. Leave those assignments blank. Where a cavity has repeated gauge entries, retain both rows without inventing an applicability rule.

The summary’s Pin Count disagrees with the numbered range shown in the drawing; the supplied evidence does not reconcile that difference. This page supports identification and map reading, not physical access, connector release, probing, wire selection or a diagnostic verdict. Physical viewing direction, gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes are not explained here.

edits.why: I match the harness identification before interpreting the cavity layout. The central rectangular housing feature and the projections around the perimeter provide landmarks in the printed drawing. Their appearance alone does not identify release mechanisms or establish the physical viewing direction.

The table connects each printed cavity label with its recorded circuit and function. Read complete rows so that similar lighting, lock and ground descriptions keep their distinctions, including the additional right-side ground-point designation and the passenger-door exclusion. Preserve every fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative. Blank circuit rows are unassigned in this map, and repeated gauge rows remain separate reference entries; neither supplies an electrical test result or a repair decision.

originalAuthorHold: The summary states Pin Count 37, while the supplied face drawing labels cavities 1–36 and the supplied assignment rows extend through cavity 36. The supplied evidence does not reconcile the summary count with the illustrated range; do not invent an additional cavity.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 57 primary units including complete raw-text u57 omitted from the original first CLI chunk coverage, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 2 edits. Public fields unchanged from original author; count and repeated supply gauge assignment ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
